model_meta.description: Inferred concept model of a bearing assembly with rolling support and contamination-resistant nested seals.

subsystems.description: Supports the outer ring and provides the mating spherical interface and groove for optional surface sealing.
Ring mounted at least partially in the housing; provides an inner raceway/sliding surface and spherical outer interface.
Ring mounted at least partially within the outer ring and supported for rotation by rolling elements.
Plural rolling elements in the bearing space support inner-ring rotation about an axis.

Inboard seal structure comprising a first washer fixed to one of the inner or outer rings and a first sealing member mounted to it, in sliding contact with the other ring. Its multi-lip seal is nested with the outboard seal so its axially outermost lip lies axially outward of the outboard seal's axially innermost lip. Claim 2: the first washer and outboard second sealing member cooperate to define a seal lubrication zone extending partly within bearing space. Claim 3: the washer is secured in a stepped ring portion and has an angled portion extending into bearing space; this cooperates with an angled portion of the outboard sealing member. Claim 4: flexible lip ends are flexed axially outwardly against the rings.

ports.name: Seal sliding contact with the opposite ring

subsystems.description: Outboard seal adjacent to and axially outward from the inboard seal; its second washer is fixed to the other ring and carries a second sealing member in sliding contact with the ring associated with the first washer. Its innermost lip is axially inward of the inboard seal's outermost lip. The outboard sealing member cooperates with the first washer to bound the claim-2 seal lubrication zone; claim 3 adds cooperating angled portions.

ports.name: Seal sliding contact with the complementary ring

subsystems.description: Optional surface seal fitted in a housing groove and pressed against the outer surface of the outer ring; it protects the spherical interface from contaminants and retains lubricant placed at that spherical interface.

item_flows.name: Mechanical contact relationships
item_flows.notes: Represents the expressly described rolling support and seal/surface-seal contacts.

requirements.statement: Support rotation of the inner ring about an axis using rolling elements in the bearing space.
Provide inboard and outboard seal structures that impede contaminant entry into the rolling-element lubrication zone.
requirements.rationale: Claim 1 specifies nested multi-lip inboard and outboard seals in sliding contact with opposite-ring surfaces; the detailed description says the seals create a difficult passageway that impedes contaminants from entering the rolling-element lubrication zone.

requirements.statement: Define a seal lubrication zone partly within bearing space using the first washer and outboard second sealing member, with claim-3 stepped-ring and angled portions.
In claim 6's alternate arrangement, portions of the two sealing contact zones are radially aligned, and a diagonal portion of one washer is radially aligned with those portions.

steps.description: Rolling elements occupy the bearing space between rings.
Rolling elements support rotation of the inner ring about an axis.
Inboard and outboard multi-lip seals contact the respective opposite-ring sliding surfaces.
The nested seal structures form a difficult passageway that impedes contaminants from entering the rolling-element lubrication zone.
Lubrication material such as grease is present in the seal lubrication zone between the inboard and outboard seals.
Sealing members retain the grease, lubricating seal lips and adding a contamination barrier.
